summary: Clarion County Courthouse clock tower, finished 1885 and NRHP-listed in 1979; a 1920 newspaper said it would serve as a fire lookout that fall.

facts.design: Queen Anne style courthouse with a clock tower

events.note: Courthouse completed October 14, 1885, after construction began July 6, 1883
Newspaper reported the courthouse tower would serve as a fall 1920 forest-fire lookout post, with county permission
Added to the National Register of Historic Places
Renovation begun in 2001 found serious deterioration in the clock tower

evidence.supports: courthouse tower to be used as a fall fire lookout post, run by Forester Zerby
evidence.quote: The tower of the Clarion county courthouse will be used as a lookout post for the location of forest fires this fall by Forester Zerby.
The courthouse was built between 1883 and 1885

evidence.supports: construction dates and completion on October 14, 1885
evidence.quote: Construction started on July 6, 1883 and was scheduled to be completed on November 16, 1884, but actual completion was on October 14, 1885.

evidence.supports: two earlier courthouses on the site, both destroyed by fire
evidence.quote: Both were built of brick and both were destroyed by fire.
The second courthouse burned down on September 12, 1882.

evidence.supports: added to the National Register in 1979
evidence.quote: It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1979.
The present Courthouse is a variation of the Queen Anne style of Architecture.

evidence.supports: 213 feet from ground to top of tower figure
evidence.quote: the elevation from the ground to the top of the tower figure is 213 feet.

evidence.supports: renovation began 2001 and found clock tower deterioration
evidence.quote: the renovation project grew to a cost of almost $1.9 million and extended five months as serious deterioration was found in the buildings clock tower.

evidence.supports: county preparing to move out of the courthouse in April 2024 for renovation
evidence.quote: As Clarion County prepares to move everything in the Courthouse in April for an extensive renovation of the historic structure and updating building systems

evidence.supports: courthouse listed on the National Register
evidence.quote: The courthouse is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

evidence.supports: Lady of Justice figure on top of the tower
evidence.quote: The Lady of Justice continues to stand tall upon the spire.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Courthouse built 1883-1885 on the site of two earlier courthouses; the 1920 lookout notice concerns the same building's tower.

sources.title: Clarion County Historical Series: Fire Destroys First Two Clarion Courthouses

notes_for_editor: The lookout use rests on one October 1920 newspaper notice, quoted by Forest Lookouts; no later use was found. The courthouse is the same building as the record, so the record's kind is correct but the lookout is the clock tower. The 213 ft figure runs to the top of the tower figure, not to a cab floor, so no height_m is recorded. The exploreClarion article is from a sponsored section; it is used only for the April 2024 renovation plan, and completion of that work is not confirmed. No photos added.
